svg.title: Sol-Ark dongle passive Modbus tap: XIAO ESP32S3 Plus carrier schematic
svg.text: Sol-Ark 15K dongle: passive Modbus RTU tap with XIAO ESP32S3 Plus
Rev A, 2026-10-12. Refdes match docs/hardware/README.md BOM. Solid = fitted. Dashed = optional, not fitted by default. [M] = measure first (README gates G1-G14).
F1 PTC MF-R050 (0.5 A hold), inline at the DB9 joint
W1 red / W2 black: 26 AWG stranded
R1, R2 soldered AT the pads,
W3 resp / W4 req / W5 GND: 30 AWG Kynar,
CARRIER PCB1 (perfboard, ~40 x 30 mm, foam-taped in the dongle housing)
signal GND (pad 6): joins carrier GND at XIAO pad 13
1. PASSIVE BY HARDWARE: the only path from any XIAO pin to pads 9/10 is through
R1/R2 (10 kΩ at the pad). A GPIO forced to output injects ≤ 0.33 mA: the line
moves ≤ ~0.2 V. ESP32-S3 GPIO1/2 also pulse low ~60 µs at power-up (DS Table 2-2):
same bound. No TX pin is wired. Firmware: internal pull-ups OFF on GPIO1/2.
2. XIAO 5V pad IS the USB-C VBUS net. D2 blocks regulator↔host backfeed. For USB
while installed: USB isolator + DATA-ONLY (VBUS-cut) cable. Prefer OTA.
3. Do not feed 3V3 (pad 12): it is the SGM6029 buck output (discharge switch, body diode).
4. Supply budget: ~0.6 W avg, ~2.3 W peak at 12 V (bulk C3 carries Wi-Fi bursts).
VIN at SGM6029 ≥ ~3.95 V worst case at 0.4 A vs ~3.55 V needed (100 % duty).
5. Physical separation: 12 V pair (P1 pins 1-2) and signal twist (pins 4-6) are
routed apart; the keyed empty pin 3 separates them in the connector.
6. Wires: W1/W2 26 AWG stranded silicone. W3-W5 30 AWG Kynar (solid), twisted.
Anchor every joint within 5 mm (Kapton + hot-melt or UV glue).
7. Gates before connecting: pad 7 voltage (G1), pad 9/10 idle (G2), DB9 pins/
polarity (G3), 12 V under 100 Ω load (G4), DB9 GND↔pad 6 < 1 Ω (G5).
ALTERNATE A: only if pad 7 measures ≈ 5 V (gate G1)
Replaces R3/R4 (and R5/R6 are not fitted). R1/R2 stay at the pads.
Fallback instead of U3: R9/R10 22 kΩ
U3 needs a SOT-23-6 breakout to sit on perfboard.
R12 and JP1 are NOT fitted. Nothing on the carrier,
harness or connector can drive pads 9/10.
Fitting them requires an explicitly approved
pad 10 is driven by the dongle's ESP32 TX, so a
proxy would also need the dongle trace cut and a
new design review. Not part of this build.
